issues.legal_issue: The limitation period for seeking enhanced compensation does not begin to run against a claimant who lacked notice or knowledge of the award and whose entitlement to compensation became fixed only after a later determination of competing claims.
material_facts: The claimants did not participate in the inquiry leading to the compensation award and had no knowledge of it until a later proceeding resolved competing claims to the land.
The Collector had made no apportionment because ownership shares were disputed, and the claimants became entitled to compensation only when the later proceeding determined their share.
The claimants sought a reference for enhanced compensation within six weeks after learning of their entitlement.
The High Court held the reference time-barred, and the appeal challenged that ruling.
issues.conclusion: The reference for enhanced compensation was not barred by limitation, and the High Court erred in holding otherwise.
issues.legal_principle: Under Section 18(2) of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, the expression “date of the award” is not construed mechanically; under Raja Harish Chandra Raj Singh v. Deputy Land Acquisition Officer, it means the date the award is communicated to or becomes actually or constructively known by the claimant. Where entitlement to compensation is unresolved until apportionment, the claimant's right to seek enhanced compensation crystallizes when that entitlement is determined. Sections 18 and 30, read with Dr. G.H. Grant v. State of Bihar, support that conclusion.

rule.if: appeal_from_reference_limitation_ruling and award_not_communicated_or_known and compensation_entitlement_fixed_only_later and reference_filed_within_six_weeks_after_knowledge

predicates.appeal_from_reference_limitation_ruling: The proceeding is an appeal challenging a ruling that a compensation-enhancement reference was time-barred.
predicates.award_not_communicated_or_known: The claimant was not given notice of the award and did not actually or constructively know of it before a later event.
predicates.compensation_entitlement_fixed_only_late: The claimant's entitlement to receive compensation was determined only after a later resolution of competing claims.
predicates.reference_filed_within_six_weeks_after_k: The claimant sought a reference for enhanced compensation within six weeks after learning of the award and becoming entitled to compensation.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges a limitation ruling, the award was not communicated or known, entitlement was fixed only later, and the reference was filed within six weeks after knowledge, the reference is within limitation.

issues.legal_issue: A claimant may seek enhanced compensation after a separate apportionment determination fixes the claimant's entitlement where the original award made no apportionment because of competing claims.
material_facts: The landowners disputed their respective shares, so the Collector made no apportionment of compensation.
The Collector referred the competing claims for determination, and the court later determined the claimants' share.
After that determination, the claimants sought a reference for enhanced compensation.
issues.conclusion: The claimants could legitimately seek a reference for enhanced compensation after the determination fixed their entitlement to compensation.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 18 and 30 of the Land Acquisition Act, 1894, address different circumstances. Section 18 applies where a beneficiary objects to an apportionment made in the award; Section 30 applies where conflicting claims mean the Collector makes no apportionment. The Collector may refer the dispute to a court or leave the parties to a suit. In either case, the right to receive compensation crystallizes after apportionment, and a claimant may then seek enhanced compensation under Section 18. Dr. G.H. Grant v. State of Bihar supports this distinction and the resulting right to seek enhancement once entitlement is determined.

predicates.enhancement_reference_proceeding: The proceeding seeks a reference to determine whether compensation should be enhanced.
predicates.competing_claims_prevented_original_appo: Conflicting claims meant that the original decision-maker did not allocate compensation among the claimants.
predicates.later_determination_fixed_claimant_entit: A later court or suit determined the claimant's entitlement to receive a share of the compensation.

issues.definition: Where an enhancement-reference proceeding follows competing claims that prevented original apportionment, and a later determination fixes the claimant's entitlement, the claimant may seek enhancement after entitlement is fixed.

issues.legal_issue: An enhanced-compensation award may be restored when review of the reference court's basis for enhancement discloses no error.
material_facts: The reference court had enhanced the compensation and awarded related statutory additions.
The State appealed against the enhanced award.
The Supreme Court examined the basis on which the reference court had enhanced compensation and found no error in its view.
issues.conclusion: The Supreme Court restored the reference court's enhanced-compensation award.
issues.legal_principle: The Court examined the reference court's assessment in the circumstances of the case and found no error warranting its reversal. It relied on no separate statutory rule or earlier decision for this merits determination.

predicates.appeal_challenges_enhanced_compensation: The proceeding is an appeal challenging an award that enhanced compensation.
predicates.reference_court_basis_is_supported_on_re: Review of the basis for the reference court's assessment discloses no error in that assessment.

issues.definition: When an appeal challenges enhanced compensation and review discloses no error in the reference court's basis for its assessment, the enhanced-compensation award is restored.
